questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Surface Area of a Polyhedron Given the Areas of the Faces: Word Problems
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13930500/assets/9e36e33a8d00ff486762e0eafad6e1420fab27f8721c7bdd1d1d6c6062cd1332.png)

Dave unfolds a cardboard box and gets the net shown above. In the figure, the areas of two of its faces are shown. What is the total surface area of the box?
questions.worked_solution:
The net shown corresponds to a rectangular prism. The surface area of our prism consists of $2$ squares (base and top) and $4$ rectangles (side faces). 

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Surface area} & =2\times (\text{Area of the base})+4\times (\text{Area of the side}) \\  & =2\times 4+4\times 6 \\  & =8+24 \\  & =32\,{\text{ft}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13930500/assets/c241f6afc3978dfc8d1e2a048509a2e6fc7c91b0caf5ac4814a864edc3992d0c.png)

Chloe wants to paint a steel box that has the form of a rectangular prism. Two of the polygonal faces are $4\,\text{ft}\times 4\,\text{ft}$ squares. If the cost to paint the surface is $$6.50$ per square foot, how much will it cost her in total? Note that Chloe does *not* need to paint the square sides.
questions.worked_solution:
The net of our prism is the following.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13930500/assets/7b84a48933abb96f605476c6d703406227b0fe5301b1457a447cdbb3f58f0937.png)

 

$$

$$

Each side face (apart from the square faces) of our solid is a rectangle, where the base is $7\,\text{ft}$ and the height is $4\,\text{ft}.$ Therefore

$$
\text{Area of the rectangle}=7\times 4=28\,{\text{ft}}^{2}.
$$

Now, the total area of the side surfaces consists of $4$ rectangular faces. 

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Surface area of the sides} & =4\times (\text{Area of the rectangle}) \\  & =4\times 28 \\  & =112\,{\text{ft}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the cost to paint the surface is $$6.50$ per square foot, the total amount that Chloe will have to pay is

$$
112\times 6.50=$728.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13930500/assets/54212c293853632fd46716b6216a74c3579bf89349e8b2c5cefafe80e40e42cf.png)

Assuming that all side faces have the same height of $9\,\text{m}$, find the total surface area of the square pyramid above using its net.
questions.worked_solution:
The net of our pyramid is the following.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13930500/assets/09eff98ca31b4bb350e2d793dcfa6e6972de25bb3b613c898533068c36fe9a78.png)

$$

$$

First, notice that the base of the pyramid is a square with a side equal to $2\,\text{m}.$ Hence:

$$
\text{Area of the square}=2\times 2=4\,{\text{m}}^{2}.
$$

 

Each side face of our solid is triangle, where the base is $2\,\text{m}$ and the height is $9\,\text{m}.$ Therefore:

$$
\text{Area of the triangle}=\frac{1}{2}\times 2\times 9=9\,{\text{m}}^{2}.
$$

Finally, the surface area of the pyramid consists of $1$ square (base) and $4$ triangles (side faces). 

Therefore, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Surface area} & =(\text{Area of the square})+4\times (\text{Area of the triangle}) \\  & =4+4\times 9 \\  & =4+36 \\  & =40\,{\text{m}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

A manufacturer produces an unfair tetrahedral die from a plastic net, shown above. What is the total surface area of the die?
questions.worked_solution:
The net shown corresponds to a triangular pyramid. The surface area of our pyramid consists of $1$ base triangle and $3$ side triangles. 

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Surface area} & =1\times (\text{Area of base})+3\times (\text{Area of side}) \\  & =1\times 64+3\times 78 \\  & =64+234 \\  & =298\,{\text{mm}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
